title: 2008 AMC 10B Problem 14
statement: Triangle \(OAB\) has \(O=(0,0),\) \(B=(5,0),\) and \(A\) in the first quadrant. In addition, \(\angle ABO=90^\circ\) and \(\angle AOB=30^\circ.\) Suppose that \(\overline{OA}\) is rotated \(90^\circ\) counterclockwise about \(O.\) What are the coordinates of the image of \(A?\)

solutions.text:
Because \(\angle ABO=90^\circ,\) segment \(AB\) is vertical, so \(A=\left(5,\,5\tan 30^\circ\right)=\left(5,\,\tfrac{5\sqrt3}{3}\right).\)

A \(90^\circ\) counterclockwise rotation about the origin sends \((x,y)\) to \((-y,x),\) so the image of \(A\) is \(\left(-\tfrac{5\sqrt3}{3},\,5\right).\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Find \(A\) first: \(AB=OB\tan 30^\circ\) since the right angle is at \(B\)
